Content:
FINER slice over creaturecreator-generation-morphology covering two coupled subsystems under Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Morphology/: the blittable SDF program model (Sdf/), and the contour/mesh extraction internals (Extraction/). Sign convention is negative-inside / positive-outside everywhere; surface is sampled value 0 (Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Common/GenerationTolerances.cs). [Confirmed]

(1) BLITTABLE SdfProgram + OP MODEL + ALLOCATOR OWNERSHIP. SdfProgram (Sdf/SdfProgram.cs) is a sealed IDisposable owning one NativeArray<SdfOperation> (Allocator.Persistent) plus RootIndex, InfluenceRadius (max SmoothUnion blend radius + 1e-4), and an optional root potential-bound envelope (HasPotentialBounds/PotentialMinBound/MaxBound). [Confirmed] SdfOperation is a plain blittable struct: Type, child indices A/B, float3 Parameters, float4x4 Matrix, DistanceScale, MinBound/MaxBound, and bool Cullable. [Confirmed] Op types: Empty, Sphere, Box, Capsule, Ellipsoid, Transform, Symmetry, SmoothUnion. [Confirmed] Ownership: SdfProgram.Dispose disposes its NativeArray; MutableOperations is internal (builder writes before sealing); callers see a ReadOnly view. Consumers must Dispose the program (using pattern in tests). [Confirmed] A resolved part binds to one sub-program via ResolvedPartProgram (ResolvedPartSnapshot + SdfProgram), keeping detached snapshot data rather than an authored CreaturePart reference. [Confirmed]

(2) DETERMINISTIC ID-ORDERED FOLD + BODY-FIRST COMPOSITION. SdfProgramBuilder (Sdf/SdfProgramBuilder.cs) is read-only over its input (never mutates DNA). [Confirmed] Parts are folded into the creature union in ascending Id order using System.StringComparer.Ordinal regardless of Parts authoring order - the same ordering rule DefinitionCanonicalizer uses for serialization. [Confirmed] Parent hierarchy is used ONLY for world-transform resolution (CreaturePartWorldTransformResolver) and is kept separate from SDF composition order. [Confirmed] The Body spline field is composed FIRST as the primary field, then each part is smooth-unioned onto the accumulated root (previousRoot/root fold). [Confirmed] Body samples are ordered by authoritative spline order (list index), not by Id, because sample order IS the spline. [Confirmed] Within the fold each new part is SmoothUnion onto the previous cumulative root with PartUnionBlendRadius(part): a limb part's blend comes from LimbChain.BlendRadius (ShapeDefinition.SmoothBlendRadius is inert for limbs, CC-018/ADR-001), a shape part's blend is its Shape.SmoothBlendRadius; mesh-asset parts (HasMeshGeometry, CC-031) never enter the implicit field (continue). [Confirmed] Smooth unions between adjacent Body samples and adjacent derived limb metaballs use a deterministic BodySampleBlendFactor/LimbSampleBlendFactor = 0.5f of the smaller adjacent radius (no per-sample schema field). [Confirmed]

(3) SIGN CONVENTION + NON-FINITE EVALUATOR CONTRACT (+inf=outside, NaN=invalid) AND WHERE ENFORCED. CC-064 contract: +inf means outside/culled/absent (never a giant valid distance); NaN is always invalid; -inf invalid for sampling; finite is the evaluated field. [Confirmed] Fast culling (CC-063, the only runtime mode) writes float.PositiveInfinity for a skipped operation. [Confirmed] Enforcement sites verified in source+tests: (a) SdfProgramEvaluator.SmoothMin short-circuits +inf children before blending because math.lerp(b,a,h) is NaN on inf*0 - returns min(a,b); [Confirmed] (b) CubeContourResolver.InterpolateEdge guards NaN (midpoint) and +inf endpoints (clamp t to the finite endpoint) so a crossed edge with one culled endpoint never leaks NaN/out-of-range vertex; [Confirmed] (c) DensityGrid.EstimateGradient treats +inf/NaN as absent and falls back to one-sided finite differences (never +inf - +inf -> NaN); [Confirmed] (d) appearance selection must treat all-+inf candidates as absent -> default appearance, not the Body gradient (finite-body guard; the old +inf<=+inf made Body 'win'); [Confirmed via SdfNonFiniteFieldContractTests] (e) ActiveCellScanJob and the extractor replicate NormalizeSurfaceDensity which leaves +inf as +inf and NaN as NaN (Abs(NaN)<=eps is false). [Confirmed] GenerationTolerances.NormalizeSurfaceDensity: returns 0 when |d| <= ScalarComparisonEpsilon (1e-3) else the value unchanged. [Confirmed]

(4) NON-UNIFORM SCALING = MIN-AXIS distanceScale APPROXIMATION; ELLIPSOID IS NOT Cullable. A part's creature-space matrix lossyScale yields distanceScale = min(|sx|,|sy|,|sz|) and each Transform op multiplies its child's field by DistanceScale - a documented non-uniform-scaling approximation (an SDF under non-uniform scale is not a true distance; the min axis is used). [Confirmed] Culling is proof-based: an op is skipped only when it is Cullable AND its valid world AABB inflated by InfluenceRadius does not contain the point. [Confirmed] Ellipsoid and any subtree containing one are NOT Cullable, because the approximate ellipsoid field can be smaller than the AABB distance, so AABB alone is not a culling proof (SdfOperation.Cullable doc). [Confirmed] Builder sets Cullable on a Transform op only when the wrapped primitive is not Ellipsoid (AppendResolvedPrimitive: SetCullable(..., primitiveType != Ellipsoid)); SmoothUnion/Symmetry Cullable = AND of children. [Confirmed] An AABB culling site must check the Cullable flag, never bounds alone. [Confirmed]

(5) EXTRACTION DESIGN. MarchingCubesExtractor (Extraction/MarchingCubesExtractor.cs) does not carry a 256-row MC triangulation table. Rationale documented at class level in CubeTopology/CubeContourResolver: a large externally-sourced lookup table cannot be compile-verified in this environment, so extraction is built from a small, individually-reasoned topology + a per-face asymptotic decider instead. [Confirmed as stated rationale; Inference that no hidden table exists is Confirmed by reading the files - none reference a 256-row table.] Extraction path: DensityGrid.SamplePortable samples the SDF with a Burst IJobParallelFor (SdfSamplingJob) into a NativeArray<float>, batching over a scratch buffer budgeted at 8MiB; cellSize = 1/VoxelsPerUnit; origin at -bounds maxima. [Confirmed] ActiveCellBuilder runs a Burst single-threaded ActiveCellScanJob that classifies every cell once (epsilon-normalized signs; case bit c set when corner c normalized >= 0) and retains only mixed-sign cells (case != 0 and != 255) in increasing global cell index order (z-major,y,x), so homogeneous volume is never re-traversed during contour resolution and output ordering is deterministic. [Confirmed] MeshExtractionResult.ContourResolutionCallCount == MixedCellCount is asserted in tests, proving homogeneous cells never reach the resolver. [Confirmed]

Cube topology (Extraction/CubeTopology.cs) uses one self-consistent bit-interleaved corner convention: corner i (0-7) at (i&1, (i>>1)&1, (i>>2)&1) = bit0 x, bit1 y, bit2 z. [Confirmed] 12 edges connect corners differing in exactly one bit (EdgeCorners); 6 faces list 4 corners in cyclic order (FaceCorners) plus matching cyclic FaceEdges. Self-consistency is compile-time-verified by CubeTopologyTests (every edge appears in exactly 2 faces; every face edge matches a real EdgeCorners entry; corner grid offsets match corner offsets; each face has 4 distinct corners). [Confirmed]

CubeContourResolver (Extraction/CubeContourResolver.cs) builds boundary loops per cube from 8 corner densities in three steps: (1) per-face segments - a face has 0, 2, or 4 crossed cyclic edges (never 1 or 3, since sign changes around a closed cycle are even); 0 => nothing, 2 => the single valid pairing, 4 => ambiguous checkerboard resolved by AsymptoticDecider.DiagonalConnectsThroughMiddle (through-the-middle 'B' pairing groups (e0,e1)+(e2,e3); 'A' separated groups (e3,e0)+(e1,e2)); [Confirmed] (2) loop tracing - every crossed cube edge borders exactly 2 faces and is used by exactly one segment from each, so every edge-crossing point has degree exactly 2 and the segment graph decomposes into disjoint closed loops with no special-casing (a topological guarantee, asserted by a degree-2 DomainException check in TraceLoops); [Confirmed] (3) triangulation happens outside (in MarchingCubesExtractor) via fan triangulation from the first loop vertex, documented as safe/non-self-intersecting for the star-shaped loops at target resolutions and a known simplification (revisit ear-clipping only if coarse golden fixtures show self-intersection). [Confirmed]

WHY THIS ELIMINATES HOLES (delta-audit item #1): two cubes sharing a face compute the ambiguous-face decision from the exact same four corner densities, so they always agree on that face's connectivity - there is no separate per-cube table row to disagree; the decision is a direct function of shared data. Confirmed by test CubeContourResolverTests.SharedFace_BothOrientationsOfTheSameDataProduceTheSameFaceDecision which feeds the same four physical values in the two orders a neighbor cube would present and asserts equal decisions. [Confirmed]

AsymptoticDecider (Extraction/AsymptoticDecider.cs, Nielson & Hamann 1991): IsFaceAmbiguous is a pure sign test (diagonal pairs (c0,c2),(c1,c3) each same sign but disagree with each other => checkerboard) and can never be wrong regardless of values. [Confirmed] DiagonalConnectsThroughMiddle evaluates the bilinear saddle value f(u*,v*)=(v00*v11-v01*v10)/D, D=v00-v10-v01+v11; if saddle sign == the shared diagonal (v00==v11) sign the region connects through the middle, else separated. Degenerate D (bilinear planar along a direction) falls back consistently to 'separated'/false; both cubes compute identical D from identical shared corners so consistency (the only property needed to close holes) is preserved. [Confirmed]

HAND-WORKED DECIDER-CHANGES-TOPOLOGY EXAMPLES (CubeContourResolverTests + AsymptoticDeciderTests, all predicted by hand from the documented rules, not smoke tests): (a) single corner 0 inside => exactly one 3-vertex loop on its incident edges {0,4,8}; [Confirmed] (b) corners 0,3 inside with weak off-diagonal outside corners (-1,1,1,-1 top face out) => decider 'separated' => two separate corner-cutoff triangles (edges {0,4,8} and {1,5,11}); [Confirmed] (c) same sign pattern but strong diagonal (-10,1,1,-10) => decider flips 'through the middle' => ONE connected hexagonal loop using all 6 crossed edges {0,1,4,5,8,11}. So the decider's magnitude decision changes the topology for the same sign case. [Confirmed] Direct decider math pinned in AsymptoticDeciderTests: -10,-10 diagonal vs +1,+1 off-diagonal (D=-22, saddle -4.5) => through-middle true; +1,+1 vs -10,-10 (D=22, saddle -4.5, opposite sign) => false; symmetric under v00<->v11 swap; degenerate denominator returns false without NaN. [Confirmed]

WELDING + GRADIENT WINDING + ZERO-VALUE CORNERS (MarchingCubesExtractor). Vertex welding keys a shared dictionary by edge identity (lower corner's grid coords + axis), independent of which of up-to-8 cubes computed a crossing, so neighboring cubes reuse the SAME output vertex - producing a connected (welded) mesh rather than per-cube duplicated coincident vertices; this is what delivers smooth-skinning-friendly topology, not just hole closure. [Confirmed] Welding is asserted structurally by MarchingCubesExtractorTests.Extract_VertexCountIsWeldedNotPerCubeDuplicated: welded closed genus-0 mesh satisfies Euler V-E+F=2. [Confirmed] Winding: CubeContourResolver loop direction is not guaranteed outward; instead each triangle's winding is corrected independently by comparing its geometric face normal to a finite-difference gradient (EstimateGradient) at the triangle centroid from cached grid samples - a correctly wound outward triangle's normal points generally along the gradient (density increases inside->outside). This is a safe local per-triangle fix that avoids global winding arguments and avoids re-evaluating the SDF during extraction. [Confirmed] Degenerate (near-zero-area) triangles are skipped rather than emitted. [Confirmed] Zero-value grid corners: an exact normalized-0 grid corner is represented as an intersection on every incident crossed edge; ResolveVertexIndex keys by the corner identity (axis -1) using the normalized ENDPOINT value rather than comparing interpolated positions, because near-zero values yield slightly different floating-point positions across edges incident to the same corner. [Confirmed]

MeshExtractionResult (Extraction/MeshExtractionResult.cs) is plain data (positions, triangle indices, timing/accounting counters, optional angle-weighted normals) intentionally free of Unity Mesh until ToUnityMesh(); normals/UVs are Phase 4 appearance-baking concerns (design doc 8), keeping extraction independently testable. [Confirmed] ComputeAngleWeightedNormals accumulates per-vertex face normal * subtended angle, idempotent, recomputed from scratch. [Confirmed]

(6) MeshTopologyValidator (Extraction/MeshTopologyValidator.cs) meaning of watertight: IsWatertight == (NonManifoldEdgeCount==0 && BoundaryEdgeCount==0), where every undirected edge is counted by the number of triangles sharing it; count==1 is a boundary edge (a hole), count>2 a non-manifold edge (self-intersecting/duplicated). This is the actual safety net for the hand-derived contour logic (delta-audit #1): it checks 'no holes' directly on output rather than trusting derivation. [Confirmed] Tests: single triangle => 3 boundary edges, not watertight; tetrahedron => watertight with 6 total edges; sphere / overlapping spheres at target resolution => watertight; full generation via CreatureMeshGenerator (Fast culling) yields a finite, watertight mesh. [Confirmed]

(7) PARITY + DETERMINISM (CC-008). MarchingCubesExtractorParityTests assert the active-cell extractor output is byte-for-byte identical (vertex count, each position, triangle index list, bounds, mixed-cell count) to a separate reference extractor (Tests/Runtime/MarchingCubesReferenceExtractor.cs) on the same sampled grid, for sphere, overlapping spheres, empty field, and body-spline-with-limb, plus determinism across repeated Extract calls and per-mixed-cell contour-call accounting. [Confirmed] Fast-culling generation is deterministic across runs (SdfCullingModeTests.FastCulling_IsDeterministic). [Confirmed]

SIMPLIFICATIONS/ASSUMPTIONS (documented in code, keep unless requested otherwise): non-uniform SDF scaling via min-axis distanceScale; fan triangulation; face-only Asymptotic Decider handling (per-face saddle; no interior/cube-level saddle beyond the 6 faces); nearest-part appearance selection (separate subsystem); zero-measure degenerate-saddle fallback; Border/edge gradient one-sided fallback. These match the BeastMaster 'documented simplifications' invariant. [Confirmed as documented]

NOTE ON VERIFICATION SCOPE: All claims above are Confirmed from direct source reading + nearest test assertions. NO Unity/PlayMode execution was performed in this read-only pass, so runtime parity/watertight results are cited as test-asserted (source-level Confirmed), not independently re-run. Marked Confidence 0.9 (not >=0.9 upper boundary of the Confirmed+test tier is not reached because no tests were executed this session and a few derivations are single-source). Open questions: (1) whether the fan-triangulation simplification ever self-intersects at very coarse resolution (flagged for golden-fixture revisit in code); (2) whether a cube-interior (not just per-face) saddle ambiguity beyond the 6 faces is ever reachable - code documents only face-level handling; (3) the exact allowed-source-root config for SourceLinks resolution (this draft uses repo-relative paths per request; the coarse record currently reports source.unresolved diagnostics).
